probes.question: A fair coin lands heads five times in a row. What is the chance the next toss is heads?
Believing an independent outcome is "due" after a streak is called the ____ fallacy.

image.alt: A coin tumbling in the air above a thumbs-up hand against a green studio background.

body.claim: After a run of heads, the next toss of a fair coin is still 50-50.
body.why: Each toss is independent, so earlier results do not change the next one. Three heads in three tosses has a 1 in 8 chance before you start, but once two have landed, the third is still 1 in 2. Thinking tails is "due" is called the gambler's fallacy.
